newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Airlines gets up to $5 mln in DIP financing.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Airlines gets up to $5 mln in DIP financing.

text.p: Kiwi Airlines, which is presently bankrupt, received a $2.5 million installment of a $5 million debtor-in-possession financing plan, a Kiwi spokesman said.
The financing, which is in the form of a 10 percent secured note, came from an undisclosed investor group headed by a Baltimore physician, the spokesman said.
The debtor-in-possession financing plan would enable the group to gain majority control of the carrier, which is 57 percent owned by its employees, the spokesman said.
The Kiwi spokesman said the debtor-in-possession financing will be presented on November 27, 1996, in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J. at 0930 EST/1430 GMT.

Kiwi did not receive the financing from ISBRE Holding Co, the spokesman said. On November 22, Kiwi and ISBRE were making arrangements for $5 million of debtor-in-possession financing, but Kiwi has not heard from ISBRE since early November 26, the spokesman said.
Kiwi was in talks with potential investors about debtor in possession financing, since its Chapter 11 bankruptcy filed in September. Operations at the carrier were suspended on October 15.
